title: Stigmasterol, the Active Ingredient in Huanglian Decoction, Inhibits the MAOA-NF-kappaB-MLCK Pathway to Improve the Inflammation in Rats With Reflux Esophagitis.
authors: Wang, Huan; Li, Lin; Han, Jian; Li, Yan; Yang, Jun; Qiu, Wangzhong; Yao, Liuhua
journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄连解毒汤活性成分豆甾醇通过MAOA-NF-κB-MLCK通路改善反流性食管炎炎症，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) shows significant potential in treating reflux oesophagitis (RE). Huanglian Decoction (HD) is a well-known classic TCM. This study aimed to investigate the active constituents, specifically Stigmasterol and the underlying mechanisms through which HD exerts its therapeutic effects on RE. METHODS: We employed network pharmacology, metabolomics, and molecular docking to analyze the active ingredients and interaction targets of HD and RE. An in vitro model of RE was created by incubating Het-1A cells with acidified BEBM medium. The effects of HD and Stigmasterol were evaluated by measuring cell viability, levels of inflammatory factors, and expression of tight junction proteins. Finally, the validity of the in vitro findings was confirmed by assessing the esophageal damage and inflammation in RE rats. RESULTS: Network pharmacology has identified monoamine oxidase A (MAOA) as a core target of HD in the treatment of RE. Metabolomic analysis revealed Stigmasterol to be the active component of HD. Functional studies demonstrated that HD and Stigmasterol enhanced cell viability in acid-exposed conditions, mitigated inflammation, and increased the expression of occludin, claudin- 1, and ZO-1, while simultaneously reducing levels of p-p65, MLCK, and MAOA. Molecular docking revealed that stigmasterol binds to MAOA. Notably, the protective effect of Stigmasterol on Het-1A was negated by the overexpression of MAOA. Furthermore, in vivo studies demonstrated that HD and Stigmasterol improved acute RE in rats by inhibiting the MAOA/NF-kappaB-MLCK axis. DISCUSSION: This study elucidates the role and mechanism of HD in RE. However, further clinical trials are needed to assess its applicability in clinical practice. CONCLUSION: Stigmasterol, the active ingredient in HD, inhibits the NF-kappaB-MLCK pathway via MAOA, thereby reducing RE-related cellular inflammation. This research offers novel insights for RE treatment.
abstract_zh: 目的：传统中药（TCM）在治疗反流性食管炎（RE）方面显示出显著潜力。黄连汤（HD）是一种著名的经典中药。本研究旨在探讨其活性成分，特别是豆甾醇（Stigmasterol），以及HD对RE发挥治疗作用的潜在机制。方法：我们采用网络药理学、代谢组学和分子对接技术分析HD和RE的活性成分及相互作用靶点。通过将Het-1A细胞与酸化BEBM培养基孵育，建立RE体外模型。通过测量细胞活力、炎症因子水平和紧密连接蛋白表达，评估HD和豆甾醇的效果。最后，通过评估RE大鼠的食管损伤和炎症，确认体外发现的有效性。结果：网络药理学鉴定出单胺氧化酶A（MAOA）为HD治疗RE的核心靶点。代谢组学分析揭示豆甾醇为HD的活性成分。功能研究表明，HD和豆甾醇在酸暴露条件下增强细胞活力，减轻炎症，并增加occludin、claudin-1和ZO-1的表达，同时降低p-p65、MLCK和MAOA水平。分子对接显示豆甾醇与MAOA结合。值得注意的是，豆甾醇对Het-1A的保护作用因MAOA过表达而被抵消。此外，体内研究表明，HD和豆甾醇通过抑制MAOA/NF-kappaB-MLCK轴改善大鼠急性RE。讨论：本研究阐明了HD在RE中的作用及机制。然而，需要进一步的临床试验来评估其在临床实践中的适用性。结论：HD中的活性成分豆甾醇通过MAOA抑制NF-kappaB-MLCK通路，从而减少RE相关的细胞炎症。本研究为RE治疗提供了新的见解。
